subject: Follow-up: integration constraints that affect Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finedge.com>, security@finedge.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: integration constraints that affect Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Alice / FinEdge security team — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can move toward a recommended deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

Recap from our call:
- Primary constraint: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for model data + request logs. FinEdge indicated a hard requirement for CMEK for all persisted tokens and embeddings.
- Identity: company-wide SSO (SAML 2.0 IdP) + SCIM provisioning for service accounts.
- Logging: 7 years retention for audit logs with the ability to pull raw logs for audits; need write-ups of what we store in logs and retention policies.
- Network: strict egress control (only whitelisted endpoints); possible requirement for VPC peering or private link to avoid public internet egress.
- Data residency: primary region in us-west-2; potential EU tenant in future.

Immediate asks / next steps we agreed to: 
1) FinEdge to send a filled security questionnaire (we attached our one-page starter) and note any absolute blockers.
2) Security call with our infra security architect to go over KMS/HSM integration and shared responsibility. Can you propose 2 slots tomorrow or Friday?
3) FinEdge to confirm whether SCIM provisioning is needed for both developer and service accounts, or only for end-user accounts.
4) We (Redwood) will draft two recommended architectures: Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools with BYOK via KMS/HSM and private link) and Private (VPC/private control plane or on-prem) with a short tradeoff matrix by EOD Friday.

Attachments: security_questionnaire_v2.pdf (please fill), redwood_private_arch_diagram.png, mapp_roster.xlsx

Goal: determine whether Dedicated (reserved capacity) can meet the CMEK + egress restrictions, or whether Private is required. We'll also surface any features that only Private/on-prem supports (e.g., HSM module integration or air-gapped ingest).

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finedge.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finedge.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: integration constraints that affect Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Thanks Stephanie — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- CMEK/HSM: must be customer-managed keys for all persisted content (embeddings, fine-tune checkpoints, and audit logs). We prefer an HSM-backed KMS (AWS CloudHSM or external HSM connected via KMS). If Dedicated can support BYOK with our HSM, that would be acceptable; if not, Private is likely required.
- SCIM: we need SCIM for service accounts used by model deployments (so developers and CI systems), not necessarily for every end-user.
- Logs: 7-year retention is non-negotiable for audit logs; we need a tamper-evident export process for quarterly audits.
- Network: private link/VPC peering is preferred. We need a diagram of endpoints that Redwood will require so our networking team can whitelist.

We can do a security deep-dive Fri 2026-10-30 between 10:00–12:00 PT or Mon 2026-11-02 13:00–15:00 PT. Bob (bob.lee@finedge.com) from infra will join.

I'll start filling the questionnaire and return by EOD Thu.

— Alice
Alice Chen
Head of Data Platforms, FinEdge
alice.chen@finedge.com

Alice — great, thanks for the availability. Confirming the Fri slot: 2026-10-30 10:30–11:30 PT for an initial technical working session (I booked the calendar hold).

Quick notes ahead of that call so we can be efficient: 
- Rishi will outline the BYOK paths we support today and the engineering gaps for HSM direct integration. Short version: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via KMS (BYOK) with envelope encryption; HSM-attested keys are supported in Private today. We should surface exact constraints and any engineering effort estimate.
- For logs, we can provide a tamper-evident export workflow for audit windows via signed S3 exports to a customer-owned bucket. Need to confirm whether storing export manifests in AWS with CMEK meets your compliance or whether Private-hosted storage is required.
- For network egress, we will prepare a minimal list of outbound endpoints (control plane + model pulls + metrics) and a diagram of optional PrivateLink/VPC peering architecture.

Action items for Redwood (we'll deliver before the Fri call):
- Short architecture tradeoff doc: Dedicated vs Private, focused on KMS/HSM, logs, and network (one page).
- Minimal endpoint whitelist and VPC design sketch (redwood_private_arch_diagram.png).
- Filled sample SLA addendum and draft MAP with milestones for a PoC.

If anything changes on your end, please loop Bob in and reply-all.

Thanks — Stephanie

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-29T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: integration constraints that affect Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Alice / team — quick technical note ahead of the Fri call.

- BYOK options: Dedicated today supports BYOK via customer KMS keys (AWS KMS) with envelope encryption; the key material stays in your account. Direct HSM integration (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM over a hardware module) is only available in Private deployments at GA. We can run an engineering effort (estimate 4–6 sprints) to add HSM-backed wrapping keys for Dedicated but that would be a longer timeline and likely a bespoke contract.
- Logs & retention: we can configure automatic signed exports to a customer-owned S3 bucket with lifecycle rules to satisfy multi-year retention. For tamper-evidence we recommend cross-account manifests + periodic signed digests; we will capture this in the architecture note.
- Network: PrivateLink or VPC peering is feasible. Dedicated with PrivateLink will avoid public egress for model ingestion and inference calls; there are some control-plane calls that currently require HTTPS to our control plane. For fully air-gapped ingest, Private on-prem is required.

Suggested path forward for speed:
1) Short PoC using Dedicated + customer KMS (if your HSM can export keys into KMS) to validate latency and operational fit.
2) Parallel security validation on retention/export and PrivateLink to confirm whitelist and egress constraints.
3) If HSM is non-negotiable and cannot integrate with KMS, move to Private plan and scope HSM connection.

I'll bring notes and a rough work estimate to the Fri deep-dive.

— Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
